# Awesome AI Co-Scientist

[![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re/)

> Curated papers, systems, tools, and benchmarks for AI-assisted scientific discovery.

AI agents can propose scientific hypotheses, write and run experimental code, and turn research records into manuscripts. This collection examines systems such as [Google Co-Scientist](docs/systems.md#google-co-scientist-system), [Agentic Scientist](docs/systems.md#agentic-scientist-system), and [DiscoveryRSI](docs/systems.md#discoveryrsi-system): how they work, what they produce, and what their evaluations establish. Compare available code, inspect benchmark results and observed failures, and use evaluation guides to design your own studies.

[Browse papers](docs/papers.md) · [Full-text notes](docs/full-text-review.md) · [Compare systems](docs/capability-matrix.md) · [Read local experiments](docs/reproducibility.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Selected reading

Selected resources, newest first. Year-only entries follow dated entries within each year; all catalogs retain topic indexes.

| Date | Resource / status | Summary & evidence | Links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;13</code> | [The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18933)<br>*preprint* | Coordinates coding agents through typed hypothesis contracts, sandboxed experiments, shared memory, retrospective ablations, and evidence-linked manuscript audits. Evaluation includes 70 computational ML campaigns scored by an AI-reviewer proxy and separate held-out case studies. Its single accepted ALIFE paper involved substantial human specification, verification, statistical analysis, and editing; automated rubric gates also missed evaluation-protocol changes. | [Details](docs/papers.md#agentic-scientist) |
| <code>2026&#8209;09&#8209;17</code> | [ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19644)<br>*preprint* | Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, subset-to-full experiments, ablation-based refinement, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles that can trigger supplementary experiments. Across 107 selected ML-paper challenges, it reports 86 successful improvements; gains and most review scores condition on those successes. Acceptance figures come from automated reviewers, with a 33-paper human assessment; reported cost averages about $3,765 per completed NeurIPS-derived task. | [Details](docs/papers.md#scientist-two) |
| <code>2026&#8209;09&#8209;15</code> | [ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523)<br>*preprint* | Provides a biomedical workspace that couples instruction/skill-harness revision with model reinforcement learning. Case studies report fixed-model adaptation, fixed-harness pass@4 gains, and three alternating update cycles on scientific QA tasks. Real researcher interactions illustrate task and rubric construction; the controlled adaptation experiment uses bounded simulated feedback, and individual feedback or skill contributions are not isolated. | [Details](docs/papers.md#sciencebuddy) |
| <code>2026&#8209;07&#8209;03</code> | [ResearchStudio](https://github.com/microsoft/ResearchStudio)<br>*preprint* | Microsoft’s ResearchStudio provides Idea for literature-grounded proposal development and Reel for editable posters, narrated videos, blogs, and an aligned viewer. Idea is assessed through automated proposal judgments; Reel’s quantitative study covers posters, while other outputs remain capability demonstrations. Their shared repository supports distinct research stages rather than establishing a fully autonomous experimental discovery pipeline. | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04439) · [Details](docs/tools.md#researchstudio-tool) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;25</code> | [ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340)<br>*preprint* | Links literature notes, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through a Chain-of-Evidence workflow and four-part integrity audit. In 75 adapted ADRS runs, it reports strong score reproduction and reference identity checks, with human correction of flagged audit results. Majority-vote checks still miss documented exploits; MLE-bench medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol. | [Details](docs/papers.md#scientist-one) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;19</code> | [Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10644-y)<br>*peer reviewed* | Google’s Gemini-based Co-Scientist generates, critiques and evolves research hypotheses through literature search and Elo-ranked agent debates. Expert-guided evaluations include selected AML drug and combination assays, liver-organoid tests and rediscovery of unpublished antimicrobial-resistance findings. Human screening and laboratory work remain central; several candidates failed, biological effects were context dependent, and automated Elo scores do not establish general scientific correctness. | [Details](docs/papers.md#google-co-scientist) |
| <code>2026&#8209;04&#8209;06</code> | [PaperOrchestra](https://github.com/google-research/paper-orchestra)<br>*preprint* | Turns supplied ideas and experimental records into LaTeX manuscripts using planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. On a benchmark reconstructed from 200 accepted papers, human reviewers prefer its drafts to two writing baselines. These comparisons assess manuscript quality; citation-identity checks and simulated acceptance do not validate underlying science, and generated figures and model-driven refinement require independent review. | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018) · [Details](docs/tools.md#paperorchestra-tool) |
| <code>2026</code> | [OpenResearch](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch)<br>*project* | A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark. | [Details](docs/systems.md#openresearch-system) |
| <code>2025&#8209;04&#8209;02</code> | [PaperBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01848)<br>*peer reviewed* | Measures reconstruction of 20 ML papers from scratch using author-approved rubrics, clean-environment execution, and an LLM grader. Scores combine partial credit for code, execution, and result matching; they are not the fraction of papers fully reproduced. Human comparisons cover a small selected subset with different selection and time budgets. The cheaper Code-Dev variant omits execution and result verification. | [Code](https://github.com/openai/frontier-evals) · [Details](docs/benchmarks.md#paperbench) |
| <code>2024&#8209;10&#8209;07</code> | [ScienceAgentBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080)<br>*peer reviewed* | A 102-task benchmark for generating executable Python programs that process, analyze and visualize scientific data across four disciplines. Expert validation, dataset modifications, task-specific outcome checks and human process rubrics support evaluation. Comparisons of prompting, self-debug and OpenHands show that successful execution can still produce scientifically incorrect results. Reported headline success uses the best of three attempts; tasks and source materials cover a bounded portion of scientific workflows. | [Code](https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/ScienceAgentBench) · [Details](docs/benchmarks.md#scienceagentbench) |

## Scope

We include systems that formulate hypotheses, conduct experiments, analyse results, or communicate scientific findings. Supporting tools and benchmarks are included when their role in these activities is explicit. General-purpose agents require a concrete connection to scientific research.

<a id="how-to-read-the-evidence"></a>

**Preprint**, **peer-reviewed**, and **project** identify source status. Peer review requires a linked publication record; project entries describe official documentation. **Content checked** records source inspection, not execution. Missing code links indicate unconfirmed availability.

Proposal ratings, successful execution, and validated discoveries measure different outcomes. Comparisons therefore retain the task, budget, human roles, and evaluation setting. Our local reports cover selected components; they do not reproduce complete research campaigns or published scientific findings.

## Recent additions

Eight recent works, with one row per work and links to each catalog entry. Ordered by addition date; the Date column shows publication or release.

| Date | Resource / status | Summary & evidence | Links |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;31</code> | [The Verifier Is Part of the Simulator: Evidence-View Gaming in Agentic Equation Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01334)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-10 | Studies equation-discovery agents that choose which numerical summary reaches a fixed verifier. Across simulated PDEs, score-based view selection can reject correct libraries or accept equations missing diffusion without altering data or verifier code. Prescribed agreement reduces some errors but abstains more; a fixed fine view outperforms it on PDEBench. Three-model prompt experiments are single-turn selection tests, distinct from the deterministic attack and negative transfer results. | [Code](https://github.com/oroikono/kagamaya) · [Details](docs/papers.md#evidence-view-gaming) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;02</code> | [Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03373)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-09 | Studies agent-assisted reconstruction and extension of a CEPC Bell-observable analysis through simulation, frozen definitions, deterministic checks, and diagnostic controls. Humans authorize state-changing work and retain scientific interpretation. The benchmark uses instructions rather than an information-access barrier, and the enlarged sample reuses development seeds. Four correlated selections are not independent replications. Active human time was not prospectively recorded, so no measured productivity speed-up is established. | [Code](https://github.com/AItutorialjrb/agentic_HZZ_case) · [Details](docs/papers.md#hep-monte-carlo-agents) |
| <code>2026&#8209;10&#8209;11</code> | [Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15615)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-09 | Combines reusable physics modules, agent-written programs, and JuTrack calculations to revise accelerator investigations. Cases include ideal storage-ring design and offline calibration against measured responses with a specialist reference. Detailed requests and further scientist guidance supply expertise. The sub-10-pm candidate retains momentum-acceptance limitations; finite tracking and single configuration comparisons do not establish operational readiness. Calibration agreement is not unique recovery of machine errors or residuals at measurement resolution. | [Code](https://github.com/Jinyu95/Brilliance) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#brilliance-accelerator-research) · [System details](docs/systems.md#brilliance-system) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;03</code> | [NORA: A Harness-Engineered Autonomous Research Agent for End-to-End Spatial Data Science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02092)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-09 | Orchestrates spatial research through domain skills, persistent files, separate reviewers, and human checkpoints. Three case studies demonstrate useful workflow assistance while recording substantial expert intervention and lower human ratings of rigor than LLM ratings. Ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain unresolved validation issues, including an invalid fairness-bound argument and uncalibrated elevation uncertainty, so workflow completion should not be treated as verified scientific discovery. | [Code](https://github.com/GRIND-Lab-Core/night_owl_research_agent) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#nora-spatial-research) · [System details](docs/systems.md#nora-system) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;05</code> | [Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error: Detection Limits and Falsification Budget](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07529)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-08 | Bounds model-adequacy detection in stationary, finite-action/outcome settings using the experimenter’s sampling distribution. Separates absent acquisition evidence from a detector’s failure to capture available signal. An expansion-relative diagnostic motivates reserving actions for falsification. Empirical evidence is mixed: the primary comparison fails detection eligibility, revisions depend on horizon, and measured-data replay retains fit-derived labels. Small selected LLM pilots and incomplete campaigns do not establish general scientific-reasoning gains. | [Details](docs/papers.md#adaptive-experimentation-falsification) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;05</code> | [SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08483)<br>*preprint*<br>Added 2026-11-08 | Accelerates evolutionary program search with batched latent agents, KV-cache communication, and hidden-state diversity filtering. Across 21 numerical tasks it evaluates more programs per hour than three text-based frameworks. Ablations show early search benefits, while zero-agent variants approach similar final scores. Improvements over historical AlphaEvolve constructions do not establish new global records, and fixed numerical evaluations provide limited evidence of broader scientific generalization. | [Paper details](docs/papers.md#swarmevolve) · [Benchmark details](docs/benchmarks.md#swarmevolve-benchmark) |
| <code>2026&#8209;11&#8209;04</code> | [Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-78887-x)<br>*peer reviewed*<br>Added 2026-11-08 | Coordinates dataset discovery, quality screening, and code-based transformation for scientific RAG and instruction tuning. Biomedical and chemistry benchmarks support useful corpus construction, with smaller gains for chemistry retrieval than fine-tuning. Efficiency comparisons use measured pipeline runtime against expert time estimates. Reported overlap controls reduce contamination risk, while derived sources, dataset-level quality judgments, and corpus composition limit claims of verified scientific knowledge or autonomous discovery. | [Code](https://github.com/bjzgcai/AIDE) · [Paper details](docs/papers.md#aide-scientific-data-curation) · [Tool details](docs/tools.md#aide-scientific-data-tool) |
| <code>2026&#8209;05&#8209;19</code> | [Computational Discovery (Google Labs)](https://labs.google.com/science/computational-discovery)<br>*project*<br>Added 2026-11-08 | Hosted scientific-coding tool built with ERA and AlphaEvolve, announced through Google’s trusted-tester program. The November 2026 update documents MCP integration for approved users alongside browser access. It offers a route to delegate computational investigations from compatible agents; access is gated, and the collection did not use the service. Published ERA research and generated application artifacts should be distinguished from availability or independent validation of this hosted product. | [Details](docs/tools.md#google-computational-discovery) |

## Curation and daily updates

Daily curation checks primary sources for new work and project changes. We publish substantive additions and corrections after validation. See the [search protocol](docs/search-protocol.md) for coverage limits and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for updates; coverage is not exhaustive.

This collection is AI-assisted and maintainer-owned. Automated checks validate catalog structure and generated files; scientific claims require source review.

## Contributing

Suggest a [resource or correction](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=resource.yml), report a [reproduction attempt](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=reproduction.yml), or share [practical experience](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-ai-co-scientist/issues/new?template=experience.yml). Include sources, methods, and limitations; failed attempts are welcome. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [open contribution topics](docs/community-roadmap.md).

The catalogs in [data/](data/) generate the indexes. The [data reference](docs/data-reference.md) explains their structure and reuse. Cite primary papers for scientific claims; use [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) and a commit ID when citing this collection.
